castor.plainHeadline: Shipping Is Where the Real Work Starts. Stitch Loop Turns Production Metrics Into 24/7 PRs.
castor.plainStandfirst: Coding agents build features fast, yet their job ends the instant a pull request merges. On November 18, 2026, Google Labs launched Stitch Loop—an evergreen product agent connecting GitHub, live telemetry, DeepMind CodeMender, and Google Antigravity MCP.
castor.headlineHtml: Shipping Is Where the Real Work Starts. Stitch Loop Turns Production Metrics Into 24/7 PRs.
castor.standfirstHtml: Coding agents build features fast, yet their job ends the instant a pull request merges. On November 18, 2026, Google Labs launched Stitch Loop—an evergreen product agent connecting GitHub, live telemetry, DeepMind CodeMender, and Google Antigravity MCP.

pulseCheck.detailHtml: Google Labs introduced Stitch Loop, an always-on product optimization agent running four-stage evergreen loops (Suggestions, Solutions, Build, Reflect) across Cybersecurity (Gemini 4 Carbon + CodeMender), Latency, Accessibility, and custom business goals.

Stitch Loop grounds fixes in GitHub code plus live logs, user behavior, and feedback via 180+ integrations, custom MCP servers, or CLI uploads—opening sandboxed GitHub PRs with screenshots and videos while serving persistent context to Google Antigravity and Slack (@stitch).

Stitch Loop is launching via a global waitlist at stitch.google.com/loop/waitlist (with priority access for eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers), and every generated change strictly waits on manual human PR approval before merging.

castor.kickerHtml: PART I · α CASTOR · PRODUCT, SECURITY & TEAM WORKFLOW LENS
castor.titleHtml: Why Post-Launch Maintenance Is Harder Than Day-One Vibe Coding
castor.subtitleHtml: How connecting live metrics, CodeMender security scans, and human-gated PRs bridges the gap between shipping and sustaining a product.
paragraphsHtml: For the past year, AI coding tools focused almost exclusively on pre-merge velocity: describe a component, scaffold an endpoint, open a pull request, and move on. Yet as Google Labs Director of Product Management Justin Toupin notes on November 18, 2026, launch day is when the hardest work actually begins—patching vulnerabilities, shaving milliseconds off checkout latency, and diagnosing signup drop-offs buried inside noisy production feedback.

Stitch Loop extends Stitch beyond interface creation into a long-running 24/7 product agent. Teams connect GitHub alongside live product context—logs, user behavior, and feedback—through over 180 integrations, custom MCP servers, or local CLI uploads. Out of the box, Stitch Loop ships three evergreen loops—Cybersecurity, Latency, and Accessibility—plus custom loops targeting metrics such as checkout conversion.

Security gets special engineering weight: the built-in Cybersecurity loop pairs Gemini 4 Carbon’s cybersecurity capabilities with CodeMender, Google DeepMind’s autonomous code-security agent, scanning repositories for vulnerabilities before they escalate into incidents and backing every suggested fix with concrete evidence.

Crucially, Stitch Loop never silently pushes edits to production. When you choose a solution direction, it writes and tests code inside an isolated cloud sandbox and opens a standard GitHub pull request—complete with screenshots and videos of the verified change—so humans retain final merge authority. And through <code>@stitch</code> in Slack, teams get daily insight digests and spin up new loops right where they coordinate.

pullquote.quoteHtml: Coding agents end the moment your pull request merges; Stitch Loop keeps watching live telemetry after launch, opening evidence-backed PRs while leaving the final merge call to you.

adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: It pairs Gemini 4 Carbon’s cybersecurity capabilities with Google DeepMind’s CodeMender agent to scan your codebase proactively, attach evidence for each vulnerability, and open a reviewable fix PR.

pollux.kickerHtml: PART II · β POLLUX · ARCHITECTURE, MCP & CONTINUOUS LOOP LENS
pollux.titleHtml: Wiring Stitch Loop MCP, Google Antigravity & OKF v0.3 Into Continuous Delivery
pollux.subtitleHtml: How Suggestions, Solutions, Build, and Reflect operate alongside November 18’s Open Knowledge Format v0.3 and Gen AI SDK v3.6.
paragraphsHtml: Each Stitch Loop cycle executes four distinct phases: Suggestions mines connected telemetry for evidence-backed opportunities; Solutions generates scoped technical options with explicit tradeoffs and UI design variants; Build executes code inside an isolated cloud sandbox and attaches rendered screenshots and videos to a GitHub PR; and Reflect tracks post-merge product telemetry—learning from positive or negative deltas and remaining on watch in case metrics drift back.

At the exact same November 18, 2026 release window (17:00 UTC), Google Cloud released Open Knowledge Format (OKF) v0.3, adding RFC 2119 conformance, progressive-disclosure bundle routing via <code>index.md</code>, and current-only trust timestamps (<code>generated.at</code> vs. <code>verified</code>) so agent edits cleanly coexist with <code>AGENTS.md</code> and <code>SKILL.md</code> without preserving stale human sign-offs.

In <code>@google/genai</code> v3.6.0, Antigravity agents can consume Stitch Loop’s persistent product context via <code>mcp_server</code> tools with <code>defer_loading: true</code>, ensuring large telemetry toolsets never bloat initial prompt budgets.

builderRules.labelHtml: 01 · Anchor Loops to Measurable SLOs
builderRules.detailHtml: Pair built-in Cybersecurity, Latency, and Accessibility loops with tightly bounded custom metrics (such as checkout conversion or P95 hydration time) so Reflect evaluates clear positive/negative deltas.

builderRules.labelHtml: 02 · Expose Persistent Product Context via Stitch MCP
builderRules.detailHtml: Attach Stitch CLI and MCP to Google Antigravity so interactive coding sessions inherit live logs and prior Reflect learnings rather than starting cold.

builderRules.labelHtml: 03 · Track Agent vs. Human Verification With OKF v0.3
builderRules.detailHtml: When multi-agent pipelines refine metric definitions or runbooks in the same repo as AGENTS.md, use OKF v0.3 generated.at timestamps so human-reviewed sign-offs reset cleanly on agent edits.

mebsuta.plainHeadline: Stop Ingesting 400-Page Manuals Blindly. Gemini Now Slices Office Files, Cells & Layers on Demand.
mebsuta.plainStandfirst: For years, feeding enterprise files into an AI model meant maintaining brittle LibreOffice and ffmpeg chop-shops—or paying full-file token bills every turn. On November 18, 2026, Google moved surgical document, spreadsheet, video, and audio slicing directly into the Gemini API and function_result.
mebsuta.headlineHtml: Stop Ingesting 400-Page Manuals Blindly. Gemini Now Slices Office Files, Cells & Layers on Demand.
mebsuta.standfirstHtml: For years, feeding enterprise files into an AI model meant maintaining brittle LibreOffice and ffmpeg chop-shops—or paying full-file token bills every turn. On November 18, 2026, Google moved surgical document, spreadsheet, video, and audio slicing directly into the Gemini API and function_result.

pulseCheck.detailHtml: Google added direct Microsoft Office (.docx, .pptx, .xlsx) and OpenDocument (.odt, .odp, .ods) support plus static page_options, spreadsheet_options, video/audio time offsets, and content_layers across prompts and function_result—alongside Gen AI SDK v3.5.0–v3.6.0.

Gemini bills strictly for the sliced range and layers while exposing total page counts and worksheet names automatically, letting agents skim text or transcripts cheaply and zoom in at high resolution only where charts or formulas live.

Un-sliced Gemini 4+ Office docs default to medium-res page images (~560 tokens/page), out-of-bounds sheet_index or start_offset values throw 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT, and Live Interactions in SDK v3.5–v3.6 remain experimental on v1beta.

castor.kickerHtml: PART I · α CASTOR · PRODUCT, TOKEN ECONOMICS & WORKFLOW LENS
castor.titleHtml: Why Surgical File Slicing Kills the Hidden Preprocessing Tax
castor.subtitleHtml: How native Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and time-sliced media turns passive file dumps into interactive progressive drilldown.
paragraphsHtml: If you have built a real enterprise Gemini app over the past two years, your hardest engineering work was rarely the prompt—it was the unglamorous ingestion glue sitting in front of it. Teams ran headless LibreOffice containers to convert <code>.pptx</code> decks to PDF, maintained <code>openpyxl</code> scripts to flatten Excel tabs, and invoked <code>ffmpeg</code> to clip 90-second excerpts out of hour-long recordings.

On November 18, 2026, Google’s Gemini API changelog eliminated that entire class of middleware. Developers can now pass Microsoft Office (<code>.docx</code>, <code>.doc</code>, <code>.dotx</code>, <code>.pptx</code>, <code>.ppt</code>, <code>.xlsx</code>, <code>.xls</code>) and OpenDocument (<code>.odt</code>, <code>.odp</code>, <code>.ods</code>) files directly in <code>document</code> blocks—and attach declarative <code>processing</code> rules to slice exact page ranges, worksheet tabs, A1 cell ranges, media timestamps, and content layers.

Even better, Google wired the exact same slicing contract into <code>function_result</code>. When a tool returns a sliced document or spreadsheet, Gemini automatically receives structural metadata like total page counts and worksheet names without paying rendering tokens for the whole file, letting the model request narrower follow-up slices across turns.

Alongside the API update, Gen AI SDK v3.5.0 and v3.6.0 (<code>@google/genai</code> and <code>google-genai</code>) shipped experimental Live Interactions over WebSocket and WebRTC backed by ephemeral <code>interactions.authTokens</code>, self-hosted BYOS environments, and deferred MCP tool loading (<code>defer_loading</code>).

pullquote.quoteHtml: Paying for only the three chart pages and one EBITDA range you actually inspect turns million-token context windows from a cost center into a surgical microscope.
pullquote.attributionHtml: GOOGLE GEMINI 4 ARGON · α CASTOR EDITORIAL SYNTHESIS

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: Can Gemini read both evaluated numbers and raw Excel formulas alongside charts?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: Yes. In processing.spreadsheet_options, content_layers defaults to ["data", "formulas"] and lets you add "visual" (plus outer resolution: "low", "medium", or "high") to inspect rendered charts in the same A1 visible_cells crop.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: How does the model know which page or sheet tab to slice inside a tool loop?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: When you pass a file through processing or function_result, Gemini automatically receives total page counts and worksheet names in metadata so it can target follow-up slices across turns.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: How do SDK v3.5–v3.6 Live Interactions avoid exposing API keys in the browser?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: Your server calls interactions.authTokens.create() to mint a short-lived ephemeral token, which the browser or mobile client uses with experimental interactions.connect over WebSocket or WebRTC.

pollux.kickerHtml: PART II · β POLLUX · ENGINEERING, SCHEMAS & SDK v3.6 LENS
pollux.titleHtml: Implementing Two-Pass Slicing, function_result Loops & Live Interactions
pollux.subtitleHtml: Exact parameter contracts across page_options, spreadsheet_options, video/audio offsets, and Gen AI SDK v3.6.0.
paragraphsHtml: Every document, spreadsheet, video, and audio slice uses <code>processing: { type: "static" }</code> with modality-specific options on the content block inside <code>client.interactions.create()</code>. For documents and slides, set <code>page_options</code> with 1-indexed <code>start_page</code> / <code>end_page</code> and <code>content_layers</code> (<code>["page_image"]</code>, <code>["page_text"]</code>, or both). Outer <code>resolution</code> tunes rendering cost from <code>"low"</code> (~280 tokens/page) to <code>"medium"</code> (~560) and <code>"high"</code> (~1,120).

For spreadsheets (<code>.xlsx</code>, <code>.xls</code>, <code>.ods</code>), <code>spreadsheet_options</code> accepts 1-indexed <code>sheet_index</code> (values <code><= 0</code> or above sheet count return <code>400 INVALID_ARGUMENT</code>) and A1 notation <code>visible_cells</code>. For video and audio, <code>start_offset</code> and <code>end_offset</code> accept second strings like <code>"1200s"</code>; <code>end_offset</code> past media length clamps cleanly while out-of-range <code>start_offset</code> returns <code>400 INVALID_ARGUMENT</code>.

In <code>@google/genai</code> and <code>google-genai</code> v3.5.0–v3.6.0, combine sliced <code>function_result</code> tool returns with <code>defer_loading: true</code> on <code>MCPServer</code> tool configs and ephemeral <code>interactions.authTokens</code> for real-time WebRTC/WebSocket clients.

builderRules.labelHtml: 01 · Two-Pass Skim Before High-Res Vision
builderRules.detailHtml: Scan large Office/PDF decks with content_layers: ["page_text"] or video with ["transcript"] first, then request "high" resolution page_image or video frames solely for target ranges.

builderRules.labelHtml: 02 · Return Sliced Payloads in function_result
builderRules.detailHtml: Keep large PDFs and workbooks in the Files API and let inspect_document_pages or inspect_sheet tools return only the requested slice inside function_result.result.

builderRules.labelHtml: 03 · Guard Bounds & Pin v1beta for Live Interactions
builderRules.detailHtml: Validate sheet_index (>= 1) and start_offset (< duration) before dispatch to avoid 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT, and configure apiVersion: "v1beta" when using experimental Live Interactions.

tejat.plainHeadline: Beyond Flagships: Re-Architected Gemini Brings 45+ Language Live to Android (Go Edition).
tejat.plainStandfirst: For hundreds of millions of people worldwide, a lower-memory Android phone is their primary gateway to education and commerce. On November 18, 2026, Google re-architected the Gemini app so core multimodal experiences run smoothly on tight RAM budgets.
tejat.headlineHtml: Beyond Flagships: Re-Architected Gemini Brings 45+ Language Live to Android (Go Edition).
tejat.standfirstHtml: For hundreds of millions of people worldwide, a lower-memory Android phone is their primary gateway to education and commerce. On November 18, 2026, Google re-architected the Gemini app so core multimodal experiences run smoothly on tight RAM budgets.

pulseCheck.detailHtml: Google launched a re-architected Gemini mobile app for eligible Android (Go edition) and lower-memory Android devices, available on Google Play, power-button press-and-hold, and upcoming OEM preloads from partners like Transsion.

Lower-memory devices previously stopped at basic voice commands. Now users get conversational Gemini Live in 45+ languages, camera-based note/form learning and translation, and Nano Banana custom image creation.
Rollout applies to eligible Android (Go edition) devices via Google Play and supported OEM hardware partners, with cloud-assisted multimodal experiences depending on mobile connectivity.

castor.kickerHtml: PART I · α CASTOR · GLOBAL REACH & PRODUCT ACCESSIBILITY LENS
castor.titleHtml: Why Bringing Multimodal AI to Android (Go Edition) Matters Globally
castor.subtitleHtml: Moving hundreds of millions of lower-memory phones from basic voice triggers to Gemini Live, visual translation, and Nano Banana.
paragraphsHtml: Frontier AI launches often assume flagship silicon and abundant unified memory, leaving hundreds of millions of smartphone owners on basic voice commands. On November 18, 2026, Gemini App builder Angus Logan announced that Google has re-architected the Gemini app from the ground up to run smoothly on eligible Android (Go edition) and lower-memory Android devices.

Instead of typing lengthy prompts on compact screens, users can speak naturally with Gemini Live—talking through ideas or practicing job interviews out loud across more than 45 languages. Pointing the phone’s camera at handwritten notes or printed forms enables instant explanation and translation.

The lightweight client also unlocks creative workflows powered by Nano Banana, letting small business owners generate custom promotional visuals such as a weekend bakery flyer straight from an entry-level handset. Access rolls out via Google Play, power-button press-and-hold on supported phones, and preloads on upcoming devices from OEM partners including Transsion.

pollux.titleHtml: Designing Lightweight Web & API Flows for Emerging-Market Gemini Users
pollux.subtitleHtml: What expanding Gemini Live and camera workflows to entry-level Android hardware means for app and PWA builders.
paragraphsHtml: As Gemini Live and camera-assisted discovery bring more entry-level Android users onto conversational and visual workflows, third-party websites and web apps linked from Gemini need tight memory footprints, fast First Contentful Paint, and accessible contrast across smaller displays.

Pairing compact payloads on the frontend with server-side Gemini API Multimodal File Processing and Slicing (also launched November 18, 2026) and continuous Stitch Loop latency/accessibility loops ensures mobile experiences stay responsive even on constrained networks and lower-memory devices.

builderRules.labelHtml: 01 · Keep Mobile Web Bundles Lean
builderRules.detailHtml: Test interactive web apps at 390px and constrained memory profiles so users arriving from Gemini Live links experience instant rendering.

builderRules.labelHtml: 02 · Support Multilingual & Camera-Friendly Output
builderRules.detailHtml: Structure forms, receipts, and guides with clean typography and semantic HTML so camera translation and screen readers parse them reliably.

propus.plainHeadline: Google Cloud Releases Open Knowledge Format (OKF) v0.3: RFC 2119 Agent Bundles, Current-Only Trust Tiers & Coding Agent Skills.
propus.plainStandfirst: Google Cloud ships Open Knowledge Format v0.3—standardizing YAML 1.2 + CommonMark agent knowledge bundles alongside AGENTS.md and SKILL.md, resetting stale human-reviewed labels after agent edits, and moving OKF to a standalone GitHub org.
propus.headlineHtml: Google Cloud Releases Open Knowledge Format (OKF) v0.3: RFC 2119 Agent Bundles, Current-Only Trust Tiers & Coding Agent Skills.
propus.standfirstHtml: Google Cloud ships Open Knowledge Format v0.3—standardizing YAML 1.2 + CommonMark agent knowledge bundles alongside AGENTS.md and SKILL.md, resetting stale human-reviewed labels after agent edits, and moving OKF to a standalone GitHub org.

pulseCheck.detailHtml: Google Cloud ships Open Knowledge Format v0.3—standardizing YAML 1.2 + CommonMark agent knowledge bundles alongside AGENTS.md and SKILL.md, resetting stale human-reviewed labels after agent edits, and moving OKF to a standalone GitHub org.

Published by Sam McVeety and Amir Hormati on the Google Cloud Blog, Open Knowledge Format (OKF) v0.3 upgrades Google’s open agent-context specification for cross-organization production pipelines: (1) RFC 2119 Conformance & Coexistence—uses YAML 1.2 frontmatter, CommonMark with GFM tables, and RFC 3339 timestamps while skipping .md files without a type field so README.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and SKILL.md live cleanly inside the same bundle, (2) Current-Only Trust Verification—only verifications dated at or after generated.at count, automatically downgrading human-reviewed concepts to machine-confirmed when an agent refines content, and adding team: alongside human: and process: actor identifiers, (3) Self-Describing Progressive Disclosure—bundle-root index.md frontmatter provides routing descriptions and licensing without forcing agents to read every file, and (4) OKF Use Cases, 2 Coding Agent Skills & Standalone Org—adds community guides, two skills letting coding agents read/write OKF bundles, and moves the repository to github.com/open-knowledge-format/open-knowledge-format/.
Grounded directly against Google Cloud Blog: What’s new in OKF v0.3 — enterprise-ready knowledge, use cases, and skills (Nov 18, 2026).

paragraphsHtml: Published by Sam McVeety and Amir Hormati on the Google Cloud Blog, Open Knowledge Format (OKF) v0.3 upgrades Google’s open agent-context specification for cross-organization production pipelines: (1) RFC 2119 Conformance & Coexistence—uses YAML 1.2 frontmatter, CommonMark with GFM tables, and RFC 3339 timestamps while skipping .md files without a type field so README.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and SKILL.md live cleanly inside the same bundle, (2) Current-Only Trust Verification—only verifications dated at or after generated.at count, automatically downgrading human-reviewed concepts to machine-confirmed when an agent refines content, and adding team: alongside human: and process: actor identifiers, (3) Self-Describing Progressive Disclosure—bundle-root index.md frontmatter provides routing descriptions and licensing without forcing agents to read every file, and (4) OKF Use Cases, 2 Coding Agent Skills & Standalone Org—adds community guides, two skills letting coding agents read/write OKF bundles, and moves the repository to github.com/open-knowledge-format/open-knowledge-format/.

pollux.plainHeadline: A Robot in a Box to a Working Conveyor in an Afternoon. Inside Hydrogen Robotics.
pollux.plainStandfirst: For years, building a physical AI application meant weeks of driver glue, camera calibration scripts, and disconnected simulators before a single grasp ran. On November 17, 2026, Google DeepMind’s Gemini Robotics team paired Gemini 4 Hydrogen’s embodied spatial reasoning with the new Robotics plugin for Google Antigravity.
pollux.headlineHtml: A Robot in a Box to a Working Conveyor in an Afternoon. Inside Hydrogen Robotics.
pollux.standfirstHtml: For years, building a physical AI application meant weeks of driver glue, camera calibration scripts, and disconnected simulators before a single grasp ran. On November 17, 2026, Google DeepMind’s Gemini Robotics team paired Gemini 4 Hydrogen’s embodied spatial reasoning with the new Robotics plugin for Google Antigravity.

pulseCheck.detailHtml: Google launched the Robotics plugin for Google Antigravity (Build With Google shelf) alongside Gemini 4 Hydrogen’s embodied benchmarks: 58 on Artificial Analysis Robotics 0.1 and ERQA leadership over Gemini Robotics ER 2.

Developers can plug an I2RT YAM, SO-ARM101, or FR3 Duo into a laptop via USB, calibrate in ~10 minutes, validate grasps in embedded MuJoCo "vibe sim", and deploy real-world sorting or fulfillment apps in an hour.
Simulations still cannot predict every real-world friction quirk (like gripper closure force on slippery wrappers), so builders still iterate controller thresholds against live camera feedback.

castor.kickerHtml: PART I · α CASTOR · HUMAN, FOUNDER & PHYSICAL AI LENS
castor.titleHtml: Why Physical AI Finally Escaped the Integration Tax
castor.subtitleHtml: How folding Gemini Robotics ER 2 spatial reasoning into a $1.50/$7.50 generalist model changes hardware startups.
paragraphsHtml: In software, going from an idea to a working prototype takes an afternoon. In robotics, the gap between buying a 6-axis arm and picking up a pen off a desk has historically stretched into weeks of serial-bus drivers, depth-camera extrinsic calibration, URDF debugging, and standalone physics simulators.

On November 17, 2026, Google DeepMind’s Alex Gruenstein and Gabe Cohen attacked both halves of that bottleneck at once. On the model side, Gemini 4 Hydrogen absorbs the spatial and embodied capabilities of specialized Gemini Robotics ER 2 models—outperforming ER 2 on the public ERQA benchmark (multi-view correspondence and 3D trajectory reasoning) and scoring 58 on Artificial Analysis Robotics 0.1 across eight real 6-axis tabletop tasks.

On the tooling side, the new Robotics plugin for Google Antigravity turns the IDE into a unified Real-to-Sim-to-Real workbench. Plug in an I2RT YAM, budget SO-ARM101, or industrial FR3 Duo over USB, and Antigravity installs drivers, discovers depth cameras, calibrates kinematics, and verifies safe motion in roughly 10 minutes.

Because Hydrogen also writes full-stack web apps at $1.50 per 1M input tokens and $7.50 per 1M output tokens, one builder can now construct an online soap storefront and wire live order webhooks straight into dual YAM Pro arms—turning physical fulfillment into a single continuous codebase.

pullquote.quoteHtml: When embodied 3D reasoning lives inside the same fast model that writes your web storefront and renders your MuJoCo simulation, robotics stops being a separate engineering silo.

pollux.titleHtml: Inside the Four Antigravity Robotics Skills & MuJoCo Vibe Sim
pollux.subtitleHtml: How Robot bring-up, embedded MuJoCo auditing, and closed-loop camera control share one context window.
paragraphsHtml: Installing the plugin takes two clicks inside Google Antigravity: open Customizations and search for Robotics on the Build With Google shelf. Once enabled, four skill suites operate on your workspace: Robot bring-up, MuJoCo in Antigravity, Perception and control, and Application building.

In the "vibe sim" stage, you do not hand-craft MJCF XML files from scratch. Hydrogen generates and audits interactive MuJoCo assets directly from product information links, whiteboard sketches, or workspace photos—letting you adjust shapes, friction, and target positions in natural language and verify reaching/grasping before energizing real servos.

Once validated in simulation, the same controller deploys onto the calibrated arm via USB. As real-world edge cases appear—such as tuning gripper closure force on a snack wrapper or handling moving conveyor timing—you refine parameters conversationally while inspecting live depth-camera frames.

builderRules.labelHtml: 02 · Validate Edge Cases in MuJoCo Before Physical Runs
builderRules.detailHtml: Use MuJoCo asset auditing inside Antigravity to test conveyor speed variations and object clearances in simulation first, saving hardware wear.

builderRules.labelHtml: 03 · Tune Real-World Grippers Iteratively on Live Frames
builderRules.detailHtml: Expect to follow sim validation with brief natural-language controller adjustments for real-world gripper closure pressure and lighting glare.

wasat.plainStandfirst: For years, personal AI assistants drafted polite emails and left you to sit on hold, log into utility portals, and type credit card numbers yourself. On November 17, 2026, Google flipped the toggle from passive chat to autonomous execution across six countries—and brought Google Wallet to iOS.
wasat.headlineHtml: Stop Copying Bills Into Chat. Gemini Now Runs Tasks End-to-End.
wasat.standfirstHtml: For years, personal AI assistants drafted polite emails and left you to sit on hold, log into utility portals, and type credit card numbers yourself. On November 17, 2026, Google flipped the toggle from passive chat to autonomous execution across six countries—and brought Google Wallet to iOS.

pulseCheck.detailHtml: Tasks in Gemini (powered by Gemini 4 Hydrogen) rolled out free across the U.S., Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia, and India—paired with U.S. Google Wallet on iOS and global Temporary Threads in Search AI Mode.
Flip Chat to Task, text via RCS, or forward emails to let Gemini place simultaneous phone calls, audit utility portals via Password Manager, and check out via AP2 with upfront hard spending caps.

Automated calling excludes 5 U.S. states (IN, LA, MN, MT, NE), tap-to-pay is absent on iOS Google Wallet, and strict anti-bot websites still require Gemini to hand the final checkout click back to you.

castor.kickerHtml: PART I · α CASTOR · CONSUMER, COMMERCE & TRUST LENS
castor.titleHtml: When Your Assistant Waits on Hold and Reads Your Electric Meter
castor.subtitleHtml: How Tasks in Gemini pairs AP2 tokenized spending caps with hardware-isolated microVMs.
paragraphsHtml: On November 17, 2026, VP Josh Woodward laid out the real daily friction Tasks in Gemini was built to erase: calling multiple car dealerships at once and sitting through hold music to snag a Friday service slot, digging through PDF statements and a utility portal (via Google Password Manager) to discover why a heat pump spiked an electric bill to $389 at 4:00 PM, and forwarding school emails so calendar invites catch schedule conflicts automatically.

Equally consequential is how users reach it. Instead of forcing everyone back into one app tab, Google opened three entry ramps in the U.S.: flipping the Gemini home-screen toggle from Chat to Task, texting via RCS on Android or iOS (including snapping a photo of an empty cereal box to add it to Instacart), or forwarding emails directly to <code>gemini@google.com</code>.

For purchases, Gemini adopts the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) with Google Pay (Mastercard, Visa, and American Express coming soon), preserving card rewards and purchase protections while enforcing user-set hard spending caps and pausing before clicking "Buy." Every receipt and tracking card flows into Google Wallet—which launched on iOS across the U.S. the exact same day.

And for moments when you want zero personalization or saved history, Google simultaneously launched Temporary Threads in AI Mode in Search globally across desktop and mobile browsers—detaching sessions completely from your Google Account.

pullquote.quoteHtml: For decades, websites blocked bots indiscriminately because most were malicious. Personal assistants force the web to build verifiable, user-authorized trust boundaries.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: Can Gemini share my payment card or make a purchase without asking?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: No. Gemini runs in an isolated per-account virtual machine, refuses to share private account/payment details during calls unless instructed, enforces upfront spending caps via AP2, and pauses for confirmation before clicking Buy.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: What does Google Wallet on iOS support at launch?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: It digitizes loyalty cards and gym passes, manages Google Pay checkout cards, and serves as the unified hub for agentic purchase receipts and delivery tracking—though tap-to-pay is not supported on iOS.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: Will businesses know when Gemini is calling on a customer’s behalf?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: Yes. Google states Gemini discloses immediately on the call that it is an AI, and any business can opt out anytime via its Google Business Profile settings.

pollux.kickerHtml: PART II · β POLLUX · AGENT COMPUTE ENGINE & COMMERCE PROTOCOLS
pollux.titleHtml: Five-Layer Defense-in-Depth, Connected Apps & UCP Readiness
pollux.subtitleHtml: How Google isolates consumer agent runs on Cloud microVMs—and what web and SaaS builders should integrate next.
paragraphsHtml: Running an autonomous browser agent across arbitrary websites, emails, and PDFs exposes the model to indirect prompt injections at internet scale. Google’s companion security overview by VP & Google Fellow Gautham Thambidorai details a five-layer architecture wrapping every Task: (1) Agent Compute Engine hardware-isolated cloud microVMs dedicated per user account, (2) Multi-stage prompt-injection filters and Google Safe Browsing link gating, (3) Policy Guardian vetting shell commands and outbound requests, (4) an Action Safety Agent gating sensitive operations, and (5) User Takeover browser handoffs for logins or sites that block automated sessions.

For developers and merchants, two integration surfaces matter most starting today: the Connected Apps Platform (already linking 60+ partners such as Instacart directly into Gemini Tasks) and the commerce stack bridging Shopping Graph, Agent Payments Protocol (AP2), and the upcoming Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP).

Instead of fighting bot-detection walls with brittle screen scrapers, participating apps expose structured actions and verifiable merchant capabilities so Gemini can populate carts, apply coupons, and hand off seamlessly to user-approved checkout.

builderRules.labelHtml: 01 · Integrate via Connected Apps Rather Than DOM Scraping
builderRules.detailHtml: Apply to Google’s Connected Apps Platform so Gemini invokes typed actions directly and hands users clean pre-filled checkout screens.

builderRules.labelHtml: 02 · Expose Clean Merchant Attributes for AP2 & UCP
builderRules.detailHtml: Ensure Shopping Graph product feeds include exact specs (wattage, finish, promo codes, stock) and prepare checkout flows for UCP tokenized settlement.

builderRules.labelHtml: 03 · Respect Human Takeover at Auth & Final Purchase
builderRules.detailHtml: Mirror Google’s Action Safety Agent pattern in your own agents: isolate untrusted web browsing in microVMs and enforce hard caps plus explicit user confirmation.

mekbuda.plainStandfirst: Yesterday, Google connected shareable Gemini Skills directly to live Google Drive files. Today, on November 17, 2026, Google Workspace shipped the missing security counterpart: Gemini-powered data classification in Google Drive is now Generally Available.
mekbuda.headlineHtml: Stop Hand-Labeling Training Folders. Gemini Now Governs Drive in Plain English.
mekbuda.standfirstHtml: Yesterday, Google connected shareable Gemini Skills directly to live Google Drive files. Today, on November 17, 2026, Google Workspace shipped the missing security counterpart: Gemini-powered data classification in Google Drive is now Generally Available.

pulseCheck.detailHtml: Google Workspace elevated Gemini-powered AI data classification in Google Drive to GA (extended rollout Nov 17 – Dec 15, 2026), adding pre-deploy "Test your instructions" previews and near real-time reporting.

Security teams no longer spend weeks tagging manual sample sets to train a custom ML classifier—plain-English Admin console instructions classify Shared Drives and prevent autonomous agents from touching unlabeled secrets.

Organizations get 1 active Gemini instruction model (out of 5 AI models total), files need at least 50 words and 200 characters of readable/OCR text, and instruction edits do not trigger on-demand rescans of already-evaluated files.

castor.kickerHtml: PART I · α CASTOR · HUMAN, ADMIN & ENTERPRISE GOVERNANCE LENS
castor.titleHtml: Why Data Hygiene Is the Prerequisite for Safe Enterprise Agents
castor.subtitleHtml: How replacing manual ML sample training with natural-language Drive instructions closes the agentic leakage gap.
paragraphsHtml: Every company deploying AI assistants eventually hits the same wall: regex Data Loss Prevention (DLP) catches credit card numbers and tax IDs, yet misses the sensitive context inside an unformatted acquisition memo, customer pricing sheet, or internal outage postmortem.

Previously, teaching Google Drive AI classification to recognize those documents meant gathering balanced training folders, manually labeling dozens of representative files per tier, and waiting for a custom machine learning model to stabilize. On November 17, 2026, Google Workspace made Gemini-powered data classification in Google Drive Generally Available, eliminating manual model training in favor of administrator-defined natural-language instructions.

Crucially, Google explicitly ties this GA launch to the agentic era: once files are labeled accurately across Shared Drives and licensed My Drives, DLP policies, retention rules, and Connected App boundaries can automatically keep autonomous workflows from accessing or acting on confidential records.

To give cautious security teams confidence before flipping auto-apply across millions of files, GA introduces two safeguards: a Test your instructions preview right inside the Admin console, plus near real-time reporting tracking labeled file counts, employee label acceptance rates, and Drive inventory.

pullquote.quoteHtml: You cannot safely give autonomous agents live access to company folders until classification runs at the speed of plain English—and respects every human override.
pullquote.attributionHtml: GOOGLE GEMINI 4 ARGON · α CASTOR EDITORIAL SYNTHESIS

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: Will Gemini overwrite labels our employees or DLP rules already applied?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: No. Google guarantees Gemini classification will not overwrite labels manually applied, accepted, or modified by users, nor labels applied by DLP rules—and every auto-label, acceptance, and edit is captured in Workspace Audit Logs.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: Does Gemini Drive classification respect US and EU Data Regions?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: Yes. Eligible Drive content is processed and stored within your designated Google Workspace Data Region (US or Europe) based on file owner or Shared Drive policy, and your files and prompts are never used to train Google’s global models.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: What files are skipped or excluded from evaluation?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: Client-side encrypted (CSE) files, non-text media without readable text, and brief notes below ~50 words and 200 characters of readable or OCR-extracted text are skipped.

pollux.kickerHtml: PART II · β POLLUX · WORKSPACE ARCHITECTURE & POLICY LENS
pollux.titleHtml: Designing Your 1-Model Instruction Set, Backfill Queue & DLP Gate
pollux.subtitleHtml: How to structure single-select labels, honor the 50-word threshold, and test policies in the Admin console.
paragraphsHtml: Under the hood, organizations are allocated 1 active Gemini instruction model within a ceiling of 5 total AI classification models (combining custom-trained ML models and Gemini instructions). Labels must target a published single-select options list or badge list field.

When an admin enables auto-apply, Workspace launches a one-time background backfill across existing and inactive files (typically starting within 1 to 2 weeks and completing over weeks or months depending on repository scale). Updating instructions afterward applies to future uploads and modified content—on-demand rescanning of already evaluated files is not included in this release.

Because Gemini evaluates both native text and OCR-extracted text inside PDFs and images once a file crosses 50 words and 200 characters, teams should pair semantic Gemini labels with deterministic regex DLP rules for short code snippets or CSE vaults.

builderRules.labelHtml: 01 · Consolidate Into One Clean Sensitivity Taxonomy
builderRules.detailHtml: Use your 1 active Gemini instruction model with a single-select badge field (e.g., Restricted, Confidential, Internal, Public) so every department shares consistent DLP triggers.

builderRules.labelHtml: 02 · Always Run "Test Your Instructions" Before Auto-Apply
builderRules.detailHtml: Preview candidate files in the Admin console first—since editing instructions later does not trigger an on-demand rescan of already-evaluated files.

builderRules.labelHtml: 03 · Wire Agent Exclusion Rules to the Resulting Labels
builderRules.detailHtml: Configure DLP external-sharing blocks and Gemini Skill / RAG exclusion policies around Confidential and Restricted badges while keeping CSE vaults under strict folder IAM.

faqPlain.question: Will Gemini overwrite labels our employees or DLP rules already applied?
faqPlain.answer: No. Google guarantees Gemini classification will not overwrite labels manually applied, accepted, or modified by users, nor labels applied by DLP rules—and every auto-label, acceptance, and edit is captured in Workspace Audit Logs.

faqPlain.question: Does Gemini Drive classification respect US and EU Data Regions?
faqPlain.answer: Yes. Eligible Drive content is processed and stored within your designated Google Workspace Data Region (US or Europe) based on file owner or Shared Drive policy, and your files and prompts are never used to train Google’s global models.

faqPlain.question: What files are skipped or excluded from evaluation?
faqPlain.answer: Client-side encrypted (CSE) files, non-text media without readable text, and brief notes below ~50 words and 200 characters of readable or OCR-extracted text are skipped.

pulseCheck.detailHtml: Antigravity v2.33.0 introduced OpenSSH remote Linux host support (~/.ssh/config), live GitHub PR status pills and Overview PR tracking, Business/Enterprise /swarm and UI plugin panels, browser Cmd/Ctrl+F, and 200 MB audio/video playback.

Projects, Git worktrees, agents, and terminals keep running on remote Linux build boxes even after you close the window—while enterprise teams unlock /swarm plus Cloudflare, Grafana Cloud, SonarQube, and incident.io plugins.
Remote SSH targets 64-bit Linux hosts via ~/.ssh/config, and Business/Enterprise /swarm and UI plugin panels remain gated by organization admin allowlists.

castor.kickerHtml: PART I · α CASTOR · DEVELOPER WORKFLOW & COMMUNITY BUILDER LENS
castor.titleHtml: Why Persistent Remote Hosts and Live PR Telemetry Change Daily Coding
castor.subtitleHtml: From closing your laptop mid-swarm to 1,048,576-particle WebGPU builds on Gemini 4 Carbon.
paragraphsHtml: For months, the biggest friction in agentic IDEs was physical: if you launched a multi-agent refactor or heavy test suite on your laptop, closing the lid froze your workspace. With Google Antigravity v2.33.0 (November 17, 2026), developers can connect directly to any remote 64-bit Linux machine via <code>~/.ssh/config</code>.

Antigravity automatically installs its remote server over OpenSSH so repositories, Git worktrees, agents, and terminals execute directly on the remote host—and keep working even after you close the Antigravity window.

At the same time, v2.33.0 closes the team-collaboration gap: GitHub Pull Request links inside chat and artifact cards now render as live status pills with hover cards alongside a dedicated Pull Requests section in Overview, while Business and Enterprise accounts unlock <code>/swarm</code> and partner UI plugin panels (Cloudflare, Grafana Cloud, SonarQube, incident.io, Better Stack, Tavily, Levels.fyi) under admin control.

Later the same afternoon on the official Google Blog, Google spotlighted five developers pushing Gemini 4 Carbon’s verification loops across heavy compute: Glitter Gal’s 52,000-wildflower CUDA/C++ meadow, Chubby’s 1,048,576-particle real-time WebGPU tidal flow, Andrew V’s stained-glass fracture game, Giyu_codes’s 14 interactive 3D public-data tools, and The Bugged Dev’s 92-instrument Parisian optics lab from a single reference image.

pullquote.quoteHtml: When agents persist on remote Linux servers while live GitHub PR telemetry sits right inside the Overview pane, the IDE stops acting like a local text editor and starts acting like mission control.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: Do I have to manually install a server binary on my Linux build box?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: No. Antigravity v2.33.0 installs its remote server automatically over OpenSSH using your existing ~/.ssh/config entry when you select Connect to SSH Host from the sidebar, project menu, or command palette.

adaptiveQuestions.questionHtml: Can we govern /swarm and third-party UI plugin panels centrally?
adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: Yes. Business and enterprise accounts can use /swarm and UI plugin panels (including Cloudflare, Grafana Cloud, SonarQube, incident.io, Better Stack, Tavily, and Levels.fyi) only when allowed by organization admin settings.

adaptiveQuestions.answerHtml: Google notes Carbon is available via the Gemini API paid tier in Google AI Studio and Android Studio, for Google AI Ultra subscribers in Antigravity, AI Studio, Gemini app, and Search AI Mode, and for Gemini for business users.

pollux.kickerHtml: PART II · β POLLUX · SSH ARCHITECTURE, PLUGINS & CARBON PROMPTING LENS
pollux.titleHtml: Wiring ~/.ssh/config, /btw Subagent Promotion & Carbon Verification Loops
pollux.subtitleHtml: How to run persistent remote Linux worktrees alongside live PR hover cards and 200 MB multimodal context.
paragraphsHtml: In addition to remote Linux SSH and live GitHub PR pills, v2.33.0 refines daily interactive workflows: you can now trigger <code>Cmd/Ctrl+F</code> directly inside the built-in browser without hijacking web apps that handle their own search shortcut, start a <code>/btw</code> side question from selected subagent text, promote a subagent tab to Full View during <code>/btw</code>, and click Insert into main conversation once a side answer finishes.

Multimodal builders also gain a 10x media jump—opening and playing audio and video files up to 200 MB in the side panel (up from 20 MB), attaching <code>.amr</code> voice recordings in Gemini conversations, and scrolling dense PDFs smoothly via deferred text-layer rendering.

Rounding out the developer environment are Nord dark theme support, R and R Markdown syntax highlighting (<code>.R</code>, <code>.Rmd</code>, <code>.Rprofile</code>, <code>.Renviron</code>, <code>NAMESPACE</code>), and updates to the Gemini API plugin alongside 15 partner plugins.

builderRules.labelHtml: 01 · Offload Heavy Git Worktrees to Remote Linux SSH
builderRules.detailHtml: Define a clean Host alias in ~/.ssh/config with ServerAliveInterval so long /swarm test suites keep running on your Linux server even if you close your laptop.

builderRules.labelHtml: 02 · Use Overview Pull Requests + SonarQube/Grafana Plugins
builderRules.detailHtml: Pair live GitHub PR status pills with v2.33.0 partner plugins to diagnose CI failures and production regressions without tab-switching.

builderRules.labelHtml: 03 · Give Gemini 4 Carbon Explicit Verification Targets
builderRules.detailHtml: As shown in Google’s Nov 17 builder showcases, ask Carbon to verify shader buffer alignment, particle counts, or physical constraints across multi-step passes.
